answer: Invitations form a quota tree, where each identity may vouch for a fixed number of new accounts and the quota shrinks with depth. A recruit's rewards vest slowly, so the inviter carries the risk of a bad branch for many epochs. Quorum for any grade must span unrelated subnetworks. An operator who wants 1,000 seats needs a tree deep enough to trip the quota and wide enough to look diverse, and every branch sits on the ledge until vesting clears. In the nadir of a collapsed branch, the whole voyage of recruits stops paying.
